subject: Task 20.3 — F7 documentation and integration verification (Phase 20, Goal F7, ADR-024) test and test-support changes

findings.description: TQR-20.2-01 is genuinely closed, not just reworded. The 20.2 finding recorded that no test resumed a `Restoration` operation whose candidate is `Absent`, so a regression confined to `ResumeRestorationAsync` for an absent candidate would pass the suite. `RestorationWithAnAbsentBaselineIsResumedAsARemoval` seeds exactly that pair — a non-terminal `Kind=Restoration` operation with `SourcePresence=Absent` and `CandidateAfterPresence=Absent`, `candidateAfterContentSha256: null`, `sourceArtifactId: null`, `Phase=Prepared`, plus a genuine `RestorePending` state — and drives it through `_reconciler.ReconcileAsync`, i.e. the ordinary recovery gate, not a direct publisher call. I confirmed the seed is representative rather than hand-assembled: the helper builds `CaptureSession(sourceArtifact: null)` -> `CommitPublication` -> `RequestRestore` through the real `PublishedArtworkStateTransitions`, and in a throwaway probe (added under /tmp, since removed) I verified the seeded state reads back as `RestorePending` with `SourcePresence=Absent`, `SourceArtifactId=null`, `SourceFingerprint=null`, a present `ActiveImageIdentity`, and `LastOperationId=null`, the seeded operation reads back non-terminal with `ObservedAfterIdentity=null`, and `ArtworkRecoveryDecisions.Evaluate` returns `Resume` (not `CompleteAfter`) for that exact pair with the current image still present. That last point matters: the assertion is only reachable because the fake host still reports the ArrTags bytes at seed time, so a regression that short-circuited to `CompleteAfter` would be caught rather than silently passing. The durable record the test reads is genuinely the one production writes for an absent baseline (ArtworkPublisher.cs:644-660: `sourcePresence = candidateAfterPresence = state.SourcePresence`, `phase Prepared`, both artifact fields null), and the ownership token/prior-publication token are fresh tokens, which is harmless because the restoration resume path never reads them (grep over ArtworkPublisher.cs:683-900 finds no `OwnershipToken`/`PriorPublicationToken` use). TQR-20.2-01's recommended action was exactly this case, and it is now present, so the finding is closed rather than reclassified.

findings.description: The new case's assertions are isolating in the sense that matters: the removal is pinned from both directions, not just as 'not a save'. `RemoveCalls == 1` with `SaveCalls == 0` and `UpdateCalls == 0` and `CurrentBytes` nulled separates removal from save and from the item-update API, and I confirmed each leg is sensitive independently in an isolated copy. Forcing the shared mutation branch to always save (`CandidateAfterPresence == Present` -> `true`) failed the new case with Expected Completed / Actual RecoveryBlocked, proving the case fails if the absent candidate is handled as a present baseline. Forcing the item-update branch to always run (line 764 -> `true`) failed only the new case, at its `UpdateCalls == 0` assertion (Expected 0, Actual 1), so the 'removal persists its own item update' leg is pinned here too. Routing `ResumeRecoveryAsync`'s restoration branch to the publication path failed 8 cases including this one, so the case genuinely exercises the restoration resume entry. The committed assertions are not restatements: `result.OperationId == operation.OperationId` proves the seeded record was resumed rather than a fresh one created, and `IsCommitted` plus the durable `Committed` phase distinguish completion from a blocked write. The only assertions that are weaker than they look are the durable-record shape checks (`committed.Kind`, `committed.Phase`, `committed.CandidateAfterPresence`): those fields are echoed from the seed through the durable protocol and are closer to a consistency check than an independent guarantee, since the operation is re-advanced through the phases rather than re-derived. That is not a defect and it is not what carries the test, but it should not be counted as extra independent proof of the removal.

findings.description: The new case is deterministic and isolated, and it introduces no shared mutable state. The class's only statics are the read-only `Surface` and `At` fields and the pure static `Png`/`Identity` helpers; the new helper is an instance method that allocates its own capture identity and takes its bytes as a parameter, so it cannot be perturbed by another test. Each test instance owns a GUID-suffixed temp root, its own `StateRepository`, stores, publisher, reconciler, and fake host, and deletes the root on `Dispose`, and the new case uses the per-instance `_item` Guid, so there is no cross-class subject-gate contention. There is no wall-clock, filesystem-order, network, or process-state dependence: the seed uses the fixed `At` timestamp, and the production `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow` stamps are never read by an assertion. I ran the new case three times alone and the whole class three times, all green with identical counts. One honest limit on the 'restart' framing, which the worker report and the changelog both already state: unlike `CoordinatorDrivenRestorationIsResumedByTheOrdinaryRecoveryGate`, this case does not reconstruct fresh services over the state root, because the coordinator cannot create the absent-baseline operation in the first place. It is a seeded durable-record resume, not a process-kill simulation. That is accurate in the worker's own wording ('the non-terminal Restoration operation and its RestorePending state are seeded directly') and in the changelog ('synthetic persisted states'), so it is not a false claim.

findings.description: The `render-docs-state.cs` change is correctly minimal and correctly gated, and the probe claim reproduces. The diff is a single ternary around the existing status line: the non-empty branch is the original interpolated string unchanged, and only the zero-length case emits 'none'. I verified the non-empty case is byte-identical rather than assuming it — in an isolated copy I set `limitations.open` to two synthetic IDs, rendered with the old generator and with the new one, and `diff` of the two full `docs/status.md` files reported no difference (the non-empty line renders as '**Open limitations:** 2 (`F98`, `F99`); ...' under both). I also confirmed the new empty-case output is genuinely pinned by `--check` in both directions: reverting the script to the old line makes `--check` report 'stale generated blocks: status.md' with exit 2, and hand-editing the rendered line back to '0 ()' in `docs/status.md` is likewise reported stale with exit 2, so the new rendering cannot drift silently. `scripts/check-docs.sh` invokes exactly this `--check` at line 22, so the gate is the one already relied on by the documentation checks, and it currently reports the generated blocks current. The change is confined to a newly reachable state: the register had no open limitation for the first time, so the previously-dead branch is now live and the previously-live branch would have produced the malformed '0 ()'.

findings.description: Scope integrity confirmed and the coverage claims are bounded honestly. `git diff --name-only -- src/` is empty: no production behaviour moved to make a test pass, and the 14 modified files are exactly the expected test, script, and documentation surfaces plus `docs/implementation/20.3/`. I found no claim in the worker report, the changelog, the ADR-024 implementation note, or the F7 archive entry that the suite does not support. Specifically, the three recorded bounds match reality: the absent-baseline removal is genuinely not coordinator-reachable (`ArtworkGenerationCoordinator.ReadRetainedSource` returns `Failed(ArtworkSourceReadResult.Absent(...))` when `SourcePresence == Absent`, before `GenerateCoreAsync` reaches the render or the restore branch, which is what the corrected architecture/09 text now says); the two native `NoFittingBadge` cases are native-guarded and reported as explicit skips in the default suite; and no live pinned-host run belongs to Phase 20. One residual wording point for Gate 20 rather than a defect: the Phase 20 acceptance criterion in PLANS.md still says the absent-baseline removal 'is exercised by a direct publisher test with a synthetic persisted `Published` state without a baseline', which is now a floor rather than a ceiling — the direct publisher test (20.2) and the recovery-gate resume (20.3) both exist, so the criterion is satisfied and slightly understates the coverage. The phase gate is not weakened by this; the criterion was not edited by 20.3, and the added case is strictly additional evidence.

substitutes_checked: FakeArtworkHost in ArtworkReconcilerTests stands in for the Jellyfin image writer, but it does not hide the behavior under test: RemoveCalls/SaveCalls/UpdateCalls are counted separately, RemoveImageAsync nulls CurrentBytes, and the reader reports the current bytes' real hash and fixed dimensions/timestamp. The test asserts the concrete observable consequences of the removal (CurrentBytes null, the state committed Restored with a null ActiveImageIdentity) rather than a stub's return value. The real host image-mutation ABI remains host-guarded and was not exercised here.

The recovery gate is real, not a stub: the case calls ArtworkReconciler.ReconcileAsync, which reads the durable state and operation through the real stores, applies the real ArtworkRecoveryDecisions decision table, and dispatches to ArtworkPublisher.ExecuteRecoveryAsync. Only the publication leg is substituted with a renderer-free path, which is irrelevant here because no rendering occurs on the resume.

The synthetic persisted state is built through the real PublishedArtworkStateTransitions (CaptureSession -> CommitPublication -> RequestRestore) rather than hand-assembled, so the state the publisher validates is a genuine production transition. I verified independently that it reads back as RestorePending with SourcePresence Absent, no artifact, no fingerprint, a present ActiveImageIdentity, and a null LastOperationId (which is what keeps the recovery table from short-circuiting to FinalStateDurable or CompleteAfter).

The seeded ArtworkOperation matches the record production writes for an absent baseline (sourcePresence = candidateAfterPresence = Absent, phase Prepared, candidateAfterContentSha256 and sourceArtifactId null, Normal fence). Its fresh ownership/prior-publication tokens differ from the state's, which is immaterial because the restoration resume path never reads them.

No test-support substitute was added or loosened: scripts/render-docs-state.cs is a build/documentation script, not a test double, and its change is exercised by the existing --check gate rather than by a substituted assertion.

The native cases genuinely execute under the pinned oracle: the coordinator NoFittingBadge case is 1/1 with ARRTAGS_SKIA_COMPAT=1 and the recorded sysroot, and the full forced-native suite is 2014/21/2035.

The host-guarded leg was not run and is reported as unverified rather than passed, in this report and in the worker's and changelog's own bounds.
determinism_checked: Per-test isolation: each ArtworkReconcilerTests instance creates its own GUID-suffixed temp root, StateRepository, stores, publisher, reconciler, host, and per-instance item Guid, and deletes the root on Dispose. No static mutable state was added; the class's only statics are the read-only Surface and At fields and pure static helpers.

The new helper RestorePendingStateWithoutABaseline is an instance method with a parameterised byte array, so it allocates fresh capture/identity values per call and cannot observe or perturb another test's state.
No cross-class subject-gate contention: the new case uses the per-instance _item Guid, so the static ArtworkSubjectGate semaphores only serialize and cannot change an outcome.

No wall-clock, filesystem-order, network, or process-state dependence: the seed uses the fixed At timestamp and the production DateTimeOffset.UtcNow stamps are never read by an assertion. Every store read hits disk through StateRepository, so the seeded records are read from the durable files rather than from an in-memory carry-over.

Repeatability measured: the new case 1/1 three times alone, the full 26-case class 26/26 three times, the F7-focused 5-class run 103/4/107, the full default suite 1927/66/1993, and the forced-native suite 2014/21/2035 — all consistent across repeats.

sensitivity_probes_run: Probe A (ResumeRestorationAsync's `SourcePresence == Present` guard replaced with an unconditional read at ArtworkPublisher.cs:862): only RestorationWithAnAbsentBaselineIsResumedAsARemoval failed (Failed 1, Passed 25, Total 26; Expected Completed, Actual RecoveryBlocked), so the new case fails when an absent candidate is treated as a present baseline — the exact regression TQR-20.2-01 named. Reverted.

Probe B (the shared restoration mutation branch at ArtworkPublisher.cs:731 forced to always save): only the new case failed (Failed 1, Passed 25, Total 26; Expected Completed, Actual RecoveryBlocked), so the removal leg is pinned against a silent save. Reverted.

Probe C (the item-update branch at ArtworkPublisher.cs:764 forced to always persist an item update): only the new case failed, at its UpdateCalls == 0 assertion (Expected 0, Actual 1, line 481), so the 'the removal persists its own item update' leg is independently pinned. Reverted.

Probe D (ResumeRecoveryAsync line 1269 routed Restoration to the publication resume path): 8 cases failed including the new one, so the case genuinely exercises the restoration resume entry rather than passing on a generic recovery path. Reverted.

Probe E (seed-faithfulness probe, a temporary test asserting the seeded state/operation shape and the ArtworkRecoveryDecisions verdict): passed, establishing that the seed is a genuine non-terminal RestorePending pair and that Evaluate returns Resume (not CompleteAfter) with the current image present. The temporary file was created only under /tmp/final-review/test-quality and removed; the repository tree is unchanged.
summary: The 20.3 test change is one genuinely meaningful case and one correctly gated script branch, and both hold up under independent probing. RestorationWithAnAbsentBaselineIsResumedAsARemoval is not a restatement: it seeds a non-terminal Restoration with an absent candidate plus a state built through the real PublishedArtworkStateTransitions, and drives it through the ordinary recovery gate. I confirmed the seed is faithful (RestorePending, SourcePresence Absent, no artifact, present active identity, null LastOperationId) and, importantly, that the recovery decision table returns Resume rather than CompleteAfter for that pair while the current image is still present, so the mutation assertions are reachable only through the resume path. Three independent production mutations each failed exactly this case — removing the resume entry's absent-baseline guard, forcing the mutation branch to save, and forcing the item-update branch to run — and a fourth (routing the restoration resume to the publication path) failed it among 8. That closes TQR-20.2-01 as scoped. The only assertion group I would not count as independent evidence is the durable-record shape echo (Kind/Phase/CandidateAfterPresence), which the OperationId and IsCommitted assertions already cover; that is recorded, not raised as a defect. Guard honesty is intact: the test diff is 72 added / 0 removed lines, the only deleted line anywhere in the change is the generator's replaced status line, and I re-measured the reverted-file baseline at 1926/66/1992 against the committed 1927/66/1993, so the new case is +1 passed / +0 skipped with nothing dropped and no guard relaxed. The default 66 skips are unchanged, the 4 F7-focused skips are the same native-guarded cases, the native cases genuinely execute under the pinned oracle (1/1 focused, 2014/21/2035 forced-native), and the host-guarded leg is reported unverified rather than passed. The new case is deterministic and adds no shared mutable state: per-instance temp root, stores, services, host, and item Guid, a parameterised instance helper, fixed timestamps, and disk-backed reads; it passed 1/1 three times alone and the class 26/26 three times. Its one honest limit — that it seeds the record rather than reconstructing services over the state root, because the coordinator cannot create it — is stated as such by the worker and in the changelog. The render-docs-state.cs change produces byte-identical output for the non-empty case (verified by diff, not assumed) and the new empty-case output is pinned by --check from both directions, with the reverted script and a hand-edited rendered line each reported stale at exit 2; check-docs.sh invokes that same gate and currently passes. git diff src/ is empty, the 14 changed files are all expected, and every coverage claim in the worker report, changelog, ADR-024 note, and F7 archive entry is bounded by bounds I verified against source and test output. No BLOCKER or HIGH finding: the suite cannot pass while the shipped ADR-024 behaviour is broken, no skip is being counted as verification in the shipping configuration, and the one wording residual (the Phase 20 acceptance criterion now understates rather than overstates coverage) is for the Gate 20 record. PASS_WITH_FINDINGS. No test or implementation file was modified by this audit; this report is the only file written, and the orchestrator still owes the state.json reports-array step under docs/agent-contracts.md clause 5 for both the reviewer report and this one.
